spans.s: Bhujabalan-māḍai (SITI), name of a coin of the māḍai (māḍha) type. See māḍa, etc.

bhujaṅga (IA 20), an ogre. The word bhujaṅga was adopted in Javanese in the sense of a ‘pupil, disciple, scholar; a philologist, poet, literary councillor; an officially appointed professional usually residing at or near the court’. It has been suggested on this basis that Bhavadeva-bhaṭṭa's title Bālavalabhī-bhujaṅga may really mean ‘the pupil of the Bālavalabhī school’. See IHQ, Vol. XXVII, pp. 80-82.
bhujabala-māḍai , ‘a māḍai issued by a ruler named or entitled Bhujabala’; see māḍa, māḍai.
